title: Reliability and Production Readiness knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the main idea of “Reliability and Production Readiness”?
options: It removes the need to understand types or runtime behavior.
Treat external input, dependencies, credentials, error handling, observability, and recovery as production design concerns rather than afterthoughts.
It makes versioning, input validation, and testing unnecessary.
It means all Kotlin libraries and platform APIs behave identically.
questions.answer_key: Treat external input, dependencies, credentials, error handling, observability, and recovery as production design concerns rather than afterthoughts.
questions.explanation: The reliable answer is grounded in the lesson’s main principle: Treat external input, dependencies, credentials, error handling, observability, and recovery as production design concerns rather than afterthoughts. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.

questions.prompt: Which learning/debugging practice is most reliable for “Reliability and Production Readiness”?
options: Use a minimal reproducible example, compare the actual result with the expected result, and check the target/version assumptions.
Change several unrelated parts at once and keep the result that looks plausible.
Ignore warnings and suppress failures before identifying the cause.
Assume the compiler or toolchain is broken without reducing the example.
questions.answer_key: Use a minimal reproducible example, compare the actual result with the expected result, and check the target/version assumptions.
questions.explanation: A minimal reproducible example and version-aware testing separate a real behavior from a mistaken assumption. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.

questions.prompt: Which claim should a learner avoid when applying “Reliability and Production Readiness”?
options: Never inspect the official API reference for the selected target.
Treat draft or experimental features as universally stable.
Expose every internal implementation detail to every caller.
Reliability and Production Readiness removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.
questions.answer_key: Reliability and Production Readiness removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.
questions.explanation: The misconception to avoid is: Reliability and Production Readiness removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version. Review the example and one relevant edge case before moving on.
